position: Refactor in place rather than rebuild on streaming architecture, because the one-way door nature of the rebuild combined with zero roadmap slack creates unacceptable execution risk without clear evidence that streaming specifically solves the identified bottleneck.

claims.text: A one-way door architectural change coupled with no slack in the roadmap creates asymmetric downside risk: if the rebuild fails or takes longer than expected, the team has no capacity to recover or pivot.

Before committing to either refactoring or rebuilding, perform diagnostic profiling and tracing (a separate exercise from implementation) to identify the specific bottleneck; this informs whether targeted optimization is possible.

The root cause of poor pipeline performance has not yet been diagnosed; streaming architectures may or may not address it depending on whether the bottleneck stems from unbounded volume, latency requirements, or event-ordering complexity.

Switching the storage format across the entire system is irreversible and imposes substantial integration and testing burden; this cost must be justified by evidence that the current format is the fundamental limiter.

Incremental refactoring during a diagnosis phase preserves optionality longer than immediately committing to storage format change; however, each optimization layer adds coupling that makes future architectural change harder, so refactoring is not truly reversible.

assumptions: The team has not yet performed deep profiling to identify whether the bottleneck is CPU-bound, I/O-bound, memory-bound, or architectural.
The team lacks capacity to absorb a major rewrite and maintain the roadmap simultaneously.
Current storage format may be adequate for the workload, but this has not been verified through diagnosis.
Optimization headroom within the current architecture has not been quantified.
A diagnostic phase prior to implementation commitment is feasible within project constraints.
would_change_my_mind: Diagnostic evidence showing the bottleneck is inherent to the data model (unbounded volume, infeasible latency, complex event ordering).
Evidence that the team has already exhausted optimizations within the current architecture.
Proof the team has shipping experience with streaming systems and confidence in operational capability.
Confirmation the roadmap can be reset to accommodate a rebuild.
Clear cost-benefit analysis justifying storage format migration by quantified performance gains.
nuance: Both paths are one-way doors; refactoring with diagnosis is lower-commitment because you learn before irreversibly changing storage format.
